headline: Technology spending and AI initiatives are rising across most sectors while revenue trends remain mixed.
summary: Media & Entertainment shows strong AI investment but uneven revenue growth. Gaming & Lottery mixes profit pressure with expanding tech spend. Publishing & Information is split between neutral and negative performance. Education displays overall positive momentum with expanding tech projects.

industries.summary: Disney posted solid revenue growth and aggressive AI spending. WBD/Skydance cut margins and tightened spend despite a raised outlook. Versant held stable margins while expanding digital platforms.

leaders.why: Revenue up 7% to $25.2 bn and expanding AI investments

laggards.why: Operating margin down to 6.9% and revenue down 13.4%

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Multiple players are buying AI tools and filing patents to enhance content and park experiences.

themes.title: Cost discipline
themes.detail: Skydance launched a voluntary buyout program targeting $6 bn savings.

industries.it_note: Disney is expanding spend, Skydance is tightening, Versant remains stable.

industries.summary: Caesars posted higher revenue but widened losses. Bally's delivered strong top‑line growth and expanding tech spend. Light & Wonder and Brightstar showed modest margins.

leaders.why: Revenue grew 20% YoY to $792 m and expanding technology partnerships

laggards.why: Widened net loss of $123 m despite revenue rise

themes.title: Vendor & outsourcing deals
themes.detail: Bally's and Brightstar signed multiple multi‑year contracts to upgrade betting and lottery platforms.

themes.title: Margin pressure
themes.detail: Caesars' operating margin fell to 15.5% with a net loss, highlighting cost challenges.

industries.it_note: Bally's and Brightstar are expanding spend; Caesars outlook is unclear.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer added AI tools but gave no guidance change. Scholastic missed revenue and widened losses. Pearson showed accelerated growth and expanded AI acquisitions.

leaders.why: Revenue $1,779 m and expanding AI‑driven assessment capabilities

laggards.why: Revenue miss of $216.8 m and operating loss of -42.5%

themes.title: AI integration
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer and Pearson are embedding AI into tax, accounting, and assessment products.

themes.title: M&A activity
themes.detail: Scholastic plans to acquire Cottage Door Press for $71 m; Pearson made two AI‑focused acquisitions.

industries.it_note: No explicit spend guidance; AI projects are progressing but overall IT budget direction is not stated.

industries.summary: Pearson reports strong revenue growth and AI acquisitions. NYU secured multi‑hundred‑million funding for quantum facilities. SLU deepened its AI partnership with World Wide Technology.

leaders.why: Revenue $1,779 m and expanding AI assessment platform

laggards.why: Neutral impact; no recent performance data

themes.title: AI & advanced tech investment
themes.detail: NYU and SLU are partnering with tech firms to develop AI and quantum capabilities.

themes.title: Strategic acquisitions
themes.detail: Pearson bought ITS and Workera to boost AI‑driven assessment and skills verification.

industries.it_note: Multiple institutions are increasing spend on AI, quantum research and related platforms.
